parts.title: Making information understandable
questions: What kinds of information do you most often explain to other people?
Do you prefer diagrams, examples or a written list when learning something unfamiliar?
Have you seen a public notice that was hard to understand?
What makes a short explanation useful?

parts.title: Individual talk
parts.cue: Describe a piece of information you helped make easier for another person to understand.
questions: Explain why it was difficult to understand at first.
Describe what you changed in the explanation.
Say how you knew whether the change helped.

parts.title: Discussion
questions: What are the risks of leaving details out to make information shorter?
How can an organisation tell whether people understand a notice?
When is it important to offer more than one way to access the same information?
How should a public explanation handle something that is still uncertain?
